verses.text: Paul and Timothy, the servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints (holy people) in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, with the bishops (church leaders) and deacons:
Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God on every remembrance of you,
Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy,
For your fellowship (sharing) in the gospel (good news) from the first day until now,
Being confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in you will perform (keep doing) it until the day of Jesus Christ,

Even as it is meet (right) for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart, inasmuch as both in my bonds (chains), and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel (good news), you all are partakers (sharers) of my grace.
For God is my record (witness), how greatly I long after you all in the bowels (deep love) of Jesus Christ.
And this I pray, that your love may abound (grow) yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment (understanding),
That you may approve things that are excellent, that you may be sincere (pure) and without offence (fault) till the day of Christ,
Being filled with the fruits of righteousness (being right with God), which are by Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
But I would that you should understand, brothers, that the things which happened to me have fallen out (turned out) rather to the furtherance (spreading) of the gospel (good news),
So that my bonds (chains) in Christ are manifest (plain to see) in all the palace, and in all other places,
And many of the brothers in the Lord, waxing confident (growing bold) by my bonds (chains), are much more bold to speak the word without fear.
Some indeed preach Christ even of envy and strife (quarrels), and some also of good will.
The one side preaches Christ of contention (fighting), not sincerely (with an honest heart), supposing to add affliction (trouble) to my bonds (chains).
But the other side preaches of love, knowing that I am set for the defence of the gospel (good news).
What then? Notwithstanding (even so), every way, whether in pretence (pretending) or in truth, Christ is preached. And I do rejoice in this, yes, and will rejoice.
For I know that this will turn to my salvation through your prayer, and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,

According to my earnest expectation and my hope, that in nothing I will be ashamed, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also Christ will be magnified (honored) in my body, whether it be by life, or by death.
For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
But if I live in the flesh (body), this is the fruit of my labour (work). Yet what I will choose I do not know.
For I am in a strait (pulled) between 2, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ, which is far better.
Nevertheless to abide (stay) in the flesh (body) is more needful for you.
And having this confidence, I know that I will abide (stay) and continue with you all for your furtherance (growth) and joy of faith,
That your rejoicing may be more abundant in Jesus Christ for me by my coming to you again.

Only let your conversation (way of life) be as it becomes (is right for) the gospel (good news) of Christ, that whether I come and see you, or else am absent, I may hear of your affairs, that you stand fast in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel (good news),
And in nothing terrified by your adversaries (enemies), which is to them an evident token (clear sign) of perdition (destruction), but to you of salvation, and that of God.
For to you it is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on Him, but also to suffer for His sake,
Having the same conflict (struggle) which you saw in me, and now hear to be in me.

verses.text: If there is therefore any consolation (comfort) in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship (sharing) of the Spirit, if any bowels (deep love) and mercies,
Fulfil my joy, that you be likeminded (think the same way), having the same love, being of one accord (agreement), of one mind.
Let nothing be done through strife (quarrels) or vainglory (empty pride), but in lowliness (humbleness) of mind let each esteem (think of) others better than themselves.
Do not look every one on their own things, but every one also on the things of others.
Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus,
Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery (taking what was not His) to be equal with God,
But made Himself of no reputation (nothing important), and took upon Him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness (looking like) of men,
And being found in fashion (appearance) as a man, He humbled Himself, and became obedient to death, even the death of the cross.
Therefore God also has highly exalted (lifted up) Him, and given Him a name which is above every name,
That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth,
And that every tongue should confess (say openly) that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
Therefore, my beloved (dearly loved), as you have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
For it is God who works in you both to will and to do of His good pleasure.
Do all things without murmurings (complaining) and disputings (arguing),
That you may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke (fault), in the middle of a crooked and perverse (twisted) nation, among whom you shine as lights in the world,
Holding forth the word of life, that I may rejoice in the day of Christ, that I have not run in vain (for nothing), neither laboured (worked hard) in vain (for nothing).
Yes, and if I am offered (poured out) on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I joy, and rejoice with you all.
For the same cause also do you joy, and rejoice with me.
But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy shortly to you, that I also may be of good comfort (take heart), when I know your state.
For I have no man likeminded (thinking the same way), who will naturally care for your state.
For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's.
But you know the proof of Timothy, that, as a son with the father, he has served with me in the gospel (good news).
Him therefore I hope to send presently (right away), so soon as I see how it will go with me.
But I trust in the Lord that I also myself will come shortly.
Yet I supposed it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, and companion in labour (work), and fellowsoldier, but your messenger, and he who ministered (served) to my wants (needs).
For Epaphroditus longed after you all, and was full of heaviness (very troubled), because you had heard that he had been sick.
For indeed he was sick near to death. But God had mercy on him, and not on him only, but on me also, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow.
I sent him therefore the more carefully (eagerly), that, when you see him again, you may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful (sad).
Receive him therefore in the Lord with all gladness (joy), and hold such in reputation (honor),
Because for the work of Christ he was near to death, not regarding (caring about) his life, to supply your lack of service toward me.

verses.text: Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not grievous (hard), but for you it is safe.
Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision (those who only cut the body).
For we are the circumcision, who worship God in the spirit, and rejoice in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh (outward things).
Though I might also have confidence in the flesh (outward things). If anyone else thinks that they have reason to trust in the flesh (outward things), I more:
Circumcised the 8th day, of the stock (family line) of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews. As touching the law, a Pharisee.
Concerning zeal, persecuting (attacking for faith) the church. Touching the righteousness (being right with God) which is in the law, blameless.
But what things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ.

Yes doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung (garbage), that I may win Christ,

And be found in Him, not having my own righteousness (being right with God), which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness (being right with God) which is of God by faith,
That I may know Him, and the power of His resurrection (rising from the dead), and the fellowship (sharing) of His sufferings, being made conformable (made like Him) to His death,
If by any means I might attain (reach) to the resurrection (rising) of the dead.

Not as though I had already attained (reached it), either were already perfect (complete). But I follow after, if that I may apprehend (take hold of) that for which also I am apprehended (taken hold of) by Christ Jesus.
Brothers, I do not count myself to have apprehended (taken hold of it). But this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth to those things which are before,
I press toward the mark (goal) for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
Let us therefore, as many as are perfect (full-grown), be thus minded (think this way). And if in anything you are otherwise minded (think differently), God will reveal (show) even this to you.
Nevertheless, to that which we have already attained (reached), let us walk by the same rule, let us mind (think) the same thing.
Brothers, be followers together of me, and mark (watch) those who walk so as you have us for an ensample (example).
For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ,
Whose end is destruction, whose god is their belly (stomach), and whose glory is in their shame, who mind (think about) earthly things.
For our conversation (citizenship) is in heaven, from where also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ,
Who will change our vile (lowly) body, that it may be fashioned like to His glorious body, according to the working by which He is able even to subdue (bring under) all things to Himself.
Therefore, my brothers dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved.
I beseech (beg) Euodias, and beseech (beg) Syntyche, that they be of the same mind in the Lord.

And I intreat (ask) you also, true yokefellow (partner), help those women who laboured (worked hard) with me in the gospel (good news), with Clement also, and with other my fellowlabourers (fellow workers), whose names are in the book of life.
Rejoice in the Lord always. And again I say: Rejoice.
Let your moderation (gentle self-control) be known to all men. The Lord is at hand (near).
Be careful (worried) for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication (asking) with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which passes (goes beyond) all understanding, will keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honest, whatever things are just (right), whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report, if there is any virtue (goodness), and if there is any praise, think on these things.
Those things, which you have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, do. And the God of peace will be with you.
But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at the last your care of me has flourished again, in which you were also careful (caring), but you lacked opportunity.
Not that I speak in respect of want (need). For I have learned, in whatever state I am, with it to be content.

I know both how to be abased (brought low), and I know how to abound (have plenty). Everywhere and in all things I am instructed (taught) both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound (have plenty) and to suffer need.
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
Notwithstanding (even so) you have well done, that you did communicate with (share in) my affliction (trouble).

Now you Philippians know also, that in the beginning of the gospel (good news), when I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with (shared with) me as concerning giving and receiving, but you only.
For even in Thessalonica you sent once and again to my necessity (need).
Not because I desire a gift, but I desire fruit that may abound (add up) to your account.

But I have all, and abound (have plenty). I am full, having received from Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an odour (smell) of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.
But my God will supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
Now to God and our Father be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
Salute (greet) every saint (holy person) in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me greet you.
All the saints (holy people) salute (greet) you, chiefly those who are of Caesar's household (family).
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
